title: Electronic Payments for Work Permit Holders
what_it_is: Electronic Payments for Work Permit Holders

sections.label: Electronic salary payments for work permit holders
sections.summary: Electronic salary payments are mandatory for S Pass holders, but not for work permit holders, though employers must pay electronically if workers request it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Electronic salary payments were, therefore, made mandatory for S Pass holders to ensure that their employer has documentary proof of meeting the minimum salary requirement in order to enjoy the S Pass privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: MOM did consider making electronic salary payments mandatory for work permit holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: However, during our consultations with workers, employers and unions, some work permit holders expressed a preference to receive their salaries in cash as it is more convenient for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Some work permit holders also gave feedback that they would face difficulties in maintaining a minimum account balance of $500 in their bank account to avoid being charged a fee by the banks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: On the other hand, small and micro SME employers like family-run shops or mom-and-pop shops who employ work permit holders have also expressed difficulties paying salaries electronically as they would need to incur additional administrative fees and resources to do this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, our laws already require employers of work permit holders to pay salaries electronically if requested by the workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
sentences.text: Today, two-thirds of these workers receive their salaries electronically.

sections.label: Exploring comprehensive e-payment system
sections.summary: The aim is for all work permit holders to have bank accounts in Singapore, with continued consultation on a comprehensive e-payment system for salaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: In that way, we can reach 100% of the work permit holders having bank accounts here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: We will continue to consult the employers, the employment agencies and also the work permit holders to explore the possibility of making a comprehensive e-payment system for the payment of salaries.
